ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Gilda Radner Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Four weeks of bloating, early fullness and pelvic pain in a woman of 39: symptom index, pelvic examination, CA-125, and same-week imaging. Concerns: Four weeks of bloating that makes her clothes tight, feeling full after a few bites, a dull ache low in the abdomen and pelvis, and passing urine more often, on most days; she has been more tired than usual for longer than that; Afraid this is cancer: her father died of a brain tumor and ovarian cancer runs in her family; she wants to be taken seriously and told plainly. [S]

tr.td: Transvaginal ultrasound of the pelvis: a 9.2 cm solid and cystic right adnexal mass and a 5.1 cm solid left adnexal mass, both with irregular solid parts and strong internal blood flow; moderate ascites; uterus normal (O-RADS 5)

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: bilateral adnexal masses, moderate ascites, omental caking up to 4 cm, a 1.2 cm nodule on the right hemidiaphragm, and small pelvic peritoneal nodules; no enlarged lymph nodes, no liver or lung lesion, and no pleural effusion
Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the omentum: high-grade serous carcinoma, PAX8 and WT1 positive, p53 aberrant (Mullerian origin); CK7 positive, CK20 negative

Primary cytoreductive surgery by gynecologic oncology: laparotomy, total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, total omentectomy, stripping of the right hemidiaphragm peritoneum, and excision of pelvic peritoneal nodules, with no visible residual disease (complete gross resection); lymph nodes not removed because none were enlarged. Pathology: high-grade serous carcinoma of both ovaries with serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma in the right fallopian tube; omental deposit 4.5 cm, diaphragm 1.3 cm; ascitic fluid positive; pT3c, FIGO stage IIIC

Genetic counseling before germline testing: three-generation pedigree, Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry, the meaning of positive, negative and uncertain results for her and for her blood relatives, and consent for a multigene panel
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast at the end of chemotherapy: no ascites, no peritoneal or omental nodule, no enlarged lymph node, and no liver or lung lesion; expected postoperative changes (no evidence of disease)

tr.td: Urgent gynecologic oncology consultation for a suspected ovarian cancer, before any surgery, to confirm the diagnosis and plan primary treatment

At the first visit: the ovarian cancer symptom index, an abdominal and pelvic examination, CA-125 with CEA, blood count and chemistry, and a urine pregnancy test; transvaginal ultrasound and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis within the week, and image-guided biopsy if the scan shows disease outside the pelvis

Genetic counseling and germline multigene panel testing (BRCA1, BRCA2, RAD51C, RAD51D, BRIP1, PALB2 and the Lynch syndrome genes), as for every woman with epithelial ovarian cancer, and tumor testing for BRCA1 and BRCA2 and homologous recombination deficiency on the surgical specimen; if a germline variant is found, a family letter offering cascade testing to blood relatives
Primary cytoreductive surgery by gynecologic oncology aiming for no visible residual disease, with enoxaparin for four weeks after the operation

Carboplatin (AUC 5) and paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 every three weeks for six cycles, starting three weeks after surgery, after hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV screening; a three-drug antiemetic regimen on each treatment day; blood counts, kidney function and magnesium before each cycle; CA-125 each cycle; and neuropathy checks at every visit

Olaparib 300 mg twice daily as maintenance for two years after a complete response to platinum chemotherapy, chosen because the tumor carries a BRCA1 pathogenic variant; blood count monthly for the first year, with checks for fatigue, nausea, breathlessness and new cough
Surgical menopause: symptom review at each visit, non-hormonal measures, a discussion of menopausal hormone therapy at the end of treatment, and a baseline bone density scan

Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain information, a cancer support community group, and survivorship care after treatment: a visit every three months for two years with examination and CA-125, and imaging only for symptoms or a rising CA-125
Tissue diagnosis and gynecologic oncology plan within two weeks of presentation
Ultrasound, CT and biopsy within four days; diagnosis and consultation on the eighth day
Cytoreductive surgery with no visible residual disease within three weeks of diagnosis
Complete gross resection one week after the diagnosis
Six cycles of carboplatin and paclitaxel every three weeks without a delay of more than one week
Six cycles completed on schedule; CT shows no evidence of disease and CA-125 is 9
Germline and tumor genetic results available before the maintenance decision
Germline panel negative; tumor BRCA1 pathogenic variant; olaparib started
PHQ-9 below 10 throughout treatment, with a peer-support connection
